reproduction_target: Isoform-level single-cell atlas of human PBMCs generated with a bench-modified, microfluidic-free PIPseq (Fluent T20 v4.0PLUS) protocol adapted to Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing. Computational reproduction target = the analysis chain from ONT basecalling through barcode rescue and isoform quantification to the reported cell-type/isoform results: Dorado basecalling -> Python quality pre-filter -> pychopper -> custom Java Levenshtein barcode rescue into pseudo-paired-end reads -> PIPseeker -> minimap2/SAMtools alignment -> Bambu pseudo-bulk isoform discovery (NDR 0.051, Ensembl GRCh38 r113) -> gffcompare vs Glinos/Leung/Heberle annotations -> per-barcode minimap2 + Bambu quantification -> Polars matrix merge -> Java pre-filter -> AnnData QC + Scrublet -> scVI-tools AutoZI zero-inflation modelling -> kNN/UMAP/Leiden clustering and marker-based cell-type assignment -> RNApysoforms transcript-structure figures -> web-based protein analyses (ColabFold/AlphaFold2-ptm, InterProScan/CDD, SAPFIR, DeepTMHMM). Blood draw, PBMC isolation, PIPseq capture/lysis, cDNA amplification, QC, ONT library prep and PromethION sequencing are wet-lab (W, OOS for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis derived from the bioRxiv v1 full-text Methods prose. The JATS XML endpoint returned HTTP 404 (curl) / 403 (WebFetch); full text was retrieved by curl of https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.16.682832v1.full and verified to contain the title phrase 'PBMC isonome' (9 hits) before scoring. Adjacent Methods sub-sections that name a single toolchain were merged to avoid artificial inflation of |S| (minimap2+SAMtools counted once per alignment context; AnnData conversion + QC-metric filtering counted once; cell-type and T-cell sub-type assignment counted once). Tools named without any version pin in prose (Polars, the QC/clustering scanpy stack, leidenalg/igraph, RNApysoforms, SAPFIR) are scored version=0 per the Step-8 'unknown -> 0' rule, consistent with prior reports in this survey. The repo README (read as prose) names a second, separate preprocessing repository (single_cell_nextflow_pipeline) that the paper's own Data-and-code-availability statement does not list. One bounded look beyond README prose was taken - the two files under /singularity_container (pull_container.sh, single_cell_analysis_2025-03-04.def) - solely to classify capture_claim as env_lock_claimed vs container_digest_claimed; no workflow source was read. Wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: ONT basecalling: MinKNOW (23.11.4) acquisition, .fast5 basecalled with the Dorado (7.2.13+fba8e8925) GPU basecaller; passing FASTQ + sequencing_summary copied to the UK Morgan Compute Cluster
Python 3.10.13 pre-filtering script: FASTQ processed in batches of 500 files per sample/flow cell, concatenated per flow cell, reads with mean base quality < 9 removed

pychopper (2.7.10) with custom primers (Fwd_3580_partial_read1_PIP minus overhang; cPRM from Rev_PR2_partial_TSO_PIP); rescued fused reads concatenated with regular output; split into files of 8,000 reads

Custom Java (openjdk 17.0.13) tiered-barcode rescue by Levenshtein distance (discard if min distance > 2; ambiguous ties deferred; otherwise replace tier with nearest whitelist sequence) and conversion to pseudo-paired-end R1/R2 FASTQ, plus a second pass rescuing ambiguous barcodes against a per-sample master whitelist

PIPseeker (v02.01.04, Fluent Biosciences - proprietary) on pseudo-paired-end FASTQ: barcode shortening, TSO/poly-A removal, export of reads > 20bp with barcode+UMI in header, per-barcode demultiplexing, cells kept at >= 100 reads

Pseudo-bulk genomic alignment and QC with minimap2 (v2.28-r1209) and SAMtools (v1.19.2); procedure stated to be 'fundamentally the same' as the 'Read preprocessing, genomic alignment and quality control' section of Heberle et al., with deviations listed

Bambu (v3.8.1) pseudo-bulk isoform discovery and quantification against the Ensembl HG38 release-113 annotation, using the model-recommended New Discovery Rate NDR = 0.051; no ERCC spike-ins (procedure by reference to Heberle et al. 'Transcript discovery and quantification')
gffcompare (v0.12.6) of the Bambu extended annotation against the Glinos et al., Leung et al., and Heberle et al. long-read transcript annotations to call novelty

Single-cell alignment and quantification: barcode-separated FASTQ aligned with minimap2 and filtered with SAMtools as in the pseudo-bulk step, batched into groups of 300 files, quantified with Bambu using the pseudo-bulk extended annotation (discovery disabled)

Merge of per-batch Bambu output matrices with the Polars Python package into one matrix per output type (gene counts, transcript counts, transcript CPM, full-length counts, unique counts) - Polars version not pinned in prose

Initial file-size-reduction filtering with a Java script (removes cells with < 300 reads and genes expressed in < 10 cells; matrices rounded to 2 decimals and transposed) - repo step 00_Initial_Filtering; input = Bambu quantification files deposited on Zenodo

Conversion to AnnData (v0.11.3) objects, supervised QC filtering (cells/gene, genes/cell, total counts, log-counts, % mitochondrial with a 15% upper threshold, % hemoglobin; thresholds in Table S2, set per dataset from violin-plot distributions) and 'inner'-join concatenation of the two replicates
Doublet removal with Scrublet (V0.2.3): automatic thresholds computed at 0.648 (gene) / 0.642 (isoform), stringent threshold of 0.3 applied - no RNG seed reported

AutoZI zero-inflation modelling with scVI-tools (V1.2.0): batch correction on sample metadata, 20 latent dimensions, dropout 0.3, 90/10 random train/validation split, max 300 epochs, learning rate 0.01, early stopping patience 70, weight decay 0.0005; latent representations and denoised data normalized per 10,000 reads and stored in AnnData - no RNG seed reported

Clustering on AutoZI-denoised data: kNN graph with 20 neighbours per cell, UMAP dimensionality reduction, Leiden clustering (flavor = igraph) at resolutions 0.06 (cell-type) and 0.26 (sub-cell-type) - no version pinned for the scanpy/leidenalg/igraph stack, no seed reported

Marker-based cell-type and T-cell sub-type assignment: clusters labelled by co-expression of flow-cytometry marker panels (Table S4), resolution selected by cluster distinctness and marker expression patterns; markers plotted per cluster and at pseudo-bulk level - manual/supervised, no software or version named

Transcript-structure modelling and figures for known and novel isoforms with the RNApysoforms Python package (biotypes added to the extended GTF, novel transcripts labelled 'novel') - no version pinned in prose or README

Protein structure prediction with ColabFold v1.5.5 running AlphaFold2-ptm: MSAs by MMseqs2 with mmseqs2_uniref_env, templates from pdb100, dropout enabled across 8 random seeds x 5 models, 12 recycling iterations, recycle_early_stop_tolerance = 0.0, greedy pairing, unpaired_paired MSA mode, max paired:unpaired 256:512, AMBER relaxation, ranked by pLDDT/PAE - run as a web service outside the project Singularity container; specific seeds not reported

Protein domain annotation with InterProScan (v5.75-106.0) on isoform-derived protein sequences (Table S5), with Conserved Domain Database (CDD) entries cited for CD3G domains - web service outside the project container, database release not pinned
Alternative protein feature identification with SAPFIR (Sherbrooke Alternative Protein Feature IdentificatoR) for GZMB/CD3G isoform features - web service, no version and no database release pinned
Transmembrane topology prediction with DeepTMHMM (v1.0.44) supporting the secreted-vs-membrane call for CD3G-202 - web service outside the project container

headline.static_readiness: 0/21 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 8/21 computational steps (C8, C11, C12, C13, C14, C18, C19, C21) - all of them either downstream of the public Zenodo Bambu quantification deposit or operating on public annotations, and each naming an exactly-pinned tool version (gffcompare v0.12.6, Java/openjdk 17.0.13, AnnData v0.11.3, Scrublet V0.2.3, scVI-tools V1.2.0, ColabFold v1.5.5, InterProScan v5.75-106.0, DeepTMHMM v1.0.44). The remaining 13/21 steps cap at NI for two distinct reasons: (a) nine upstream steps (C1-C7, C9, C10) consume raw long-read FASTQ/fast5 that is NOT deposited - the Data and code availability statement says the raw data 'will be publicly accessible once we find a solution to host the full dataset long-term. In the meantime, it is available upon request', so the data axis is 0 there regardless of how well the code is pinned; (b) five steps (C10, C15, C16, C17, C20) name tools with no version at all (Polars, the scanpy/leidenalg/igraph clustering stack, RNApysoforms, SAPFIR) or are manual marker-based assignment. Version stays <= 1 everywhere at Stage 1 because the Singularity container is only a CLAIM here; no step can exceed RI without an executed environment capture.
headline.coverage: 21 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 full-text Methods prose plus the analysis-repo README prose. 5 wet-lab steps counted in W but out of computational-reproduction scope: (1) blood draw + Ficoll/SepMate PBMC isolation, (2) PIPseq cell preparation and cell capture/lysis (Fluent T20 v4.0PLUS, bench-modified), (3) PIPseq mRNA isolation + cDNA amplification + cDNA isolation from PIPs, (4) cDNA QC (Qubit, Agilent Femto Pulse), (5) ONT library preparation with custom oligos (SQK-PCS114 adapter addition) and PromethION R10 sequencing. Computational coverage = 21/26 = 81%.

gaps.where: Data and code availability - raw long-read scRNA-seq data
gaps.missing: No repository accession of any kind (no GEO/SRA/ENA/EGA/dbGaP id). Verbatim: 'Raw long-read scRNA-seq data generated and utilized for this study will be publicly accessible once we find a solution to host the full dataset long-term. In the meantime, it is available upon request.' Every step from basecalling through per-barcode Bambu quantification (C1-C10) therefore scores data = 0 and cannot exceed NI, no matter how exactly the tools are pinned. The Zenodo deposit (10.5281/zenodo.17341210) contains only Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.gff3.gz, PBMC_bambu_quant_files.tar.gz and four ColabFold output archives - no FASTQ, no POD5/fast5, no h5ad.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the raw ONT reads (or at minimum the aligned BAMs) under a resolvable SRA/ENA accession, or an EGA/dbGaP controlled-access accession with a documented DAC path if consent restricts open release; controlled access with a resolving accession is not penalized by the rubric, 'upon request' is.

gaps.where: Steps C10, C15, C16, C17, C20
gaps.missing: Tools named without any version pin: the Polars Python package (matrix merge), the clustering stack behind kNN/UMAP/Leiden (scanpy is never named; only 'flavor = igraph' and leidenalg are implied), RNApysoforms (transcript-structure figures), and SAPFIR (web protein-feature analysis). These cap at version = 0 -> NI even though their input data is public.
gaps.how_to_close: State an exact version for every named package in Methods or a versions table (Polars x.y.z, scanpy x.y.z, leidenalg/igraph x.y.z, RNApysoforms x.y.z, SAPFIR release/date).

gaps.where: Rigor and Reproducibility statement + /singularity_container in the analysis repo
gaps.missing: The environment-lock claim is real but not digest-anchored. The paper states 'A singularity container was used for most analyses in this study ... Instructions on accessing the singularity container used for this project can be found in the GitHub repository', and the README repeats it. The repo ships a build recipe (single_cell_analysis_2025-03-04.def) and pull_container.sh, which pulls by a mutable dated library tag ('singularity pull library://phdo222/single_cell_data/single_cell_analysis:2025-03-04'), not by digest; the .def itself bootstraps from a sha256-pinned base image but then installs most Python/R packages unpinned. Classified capture_claim = env_lock_claimed (not container_digest_claimed). Whether the shipped image actually closes the environment is a Stage-2 question.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish and cite the built image by digest (library://...@sha256:... or an OCI digest) and archive the image alongside the code, so the pull is immutable rather than tag-resolved.

gaps.missing: PIPseeker (v02.01.04) is proprietary Fluent Biosciences / Illumina software and is a hard dependency of the barcode-rescue chain; the paper also notes that the authors worked with Fluent on barcode retrieval. Proprietary dependency caps this step at NI under the rubric ceiling.
gaps.how_to_close: Document the exact PIPseeker distribution and licence path used, and/or provide an open reimplementation of the barcode-shortening/demultiplexing behaviour that downstream steps depend on.

gaps.missing: Stochastic steps with no published RNG seeds: Scrublet doublet simulation, the scVI-tools AutoZI 90/10 random train/validation split with dropout 0.3 and GPU training, UMAP/Leiden initialisation, and ColabFold's '8 random seeds' with dropout enabled. Reruns can only be matched distributionally.
gaps.how_to_close: Record and publish the seeds actually consumed (scvi.settings.seed, scanpy random_state, Scrublet random_state, the explicit ColabFold seed list) and state the torch/CUDA determinism settings used.

gaps.missing: The paper's own Data and code availability names only the analysis repository (github.com/UK-SBCoA-EbbertLab/single_cell_analysis_PBMCs). The upstream preprocessing that produces the count matrices lives in a SEPARATE repository named only in that repo's README ('This analysis utilizes count matrices generated by our Single-Cell Nextflow Pipeline, available here: https://github.com/UK-SBCoA-EbbertLab/single_cell_nextflow_pipeline'). In addition, the pseudo-bulk alignment/QC and isoform-discovery methods are specified by reference to named sections of Heberle et al. rather than restated. Neither repository carries a release tag or commit pin (GitHub tags API returns an empty list for the analysis repo), so 'the code as run' is not addressable.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the preprocessing repository in the paper itself, tag a release (or archive both repositories to Zenodo with versioned DOIs), and cite the exact commit/tag used for the reported results.

gaps.where: Steps C18, C19, C20, C21 - web-based protein analyses
gaps.missing: ColabFold (MMseqs2 mmseqs2_uniref_env, pdb100), InterProScan/CDD, SAPFIR and DeepTMHMM are explicitly excluded from the container ('with the exception of web-based analyses SAPFIR, InterScanPro, DeepTMHMM, and ColabFold') and are run against rolling remote reference databases whose release/snapshot is never pinned. Tool versions are given for three of the four, but the databases they query are mutable.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the database release identifiers queried (UniRef/ColabFoldDB build date, PDB100 snapshot, InterPro/CDD release numbers, SAPFIR build) or run the equivalent local, versioned installations inside the container.

gaps.where: Third-party comparison annotation used by step C8
gaps.missing: The Glinos et al. GTEx v9 long-read annotation URL given verbatim in Data and code availability - https://storage.googleapis.com/gtex_analysis_v9/long_read_data/flair_filter_transcripts.gtf.gz - returned HTTP 404 to an unauthenticated GET on 2026-07-28. The Leung et al. and Heberle et al. Zenodo links resolve. This is the input to the novelty calls that anchor the '128 novel isoforms' headline.
gaps.how_to_close: Re-point the Glinos annotation to a resolvable authoritative location (GTEx portal path or a Zenodo mirror) or deposit the exact comparison GTF used with the study's own Zenodo record.

gaps.missing: Blood draw and Ficoll/SepMate PBMC isolation, PIPseq cell preparation and capture/lysis, mRNA isolation and cDNA amplification/isolation, cDNA QC (Qubit/Femto Pulse), and ONT library preparation + PromethION R10 sequencing are physical sequence-generation steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W, not verdicted. Note additionally that parts of the wet-lab protocol are non-disclosable: 'Because of a legal agreement with ONT, we are unable to disclose the specific steps of these protocols', referring to the ONT single-cell and V14 protocols, which limits wet-lab reproducibility independently of the computational assessment.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness. The reproducible computational entry point would be the raw ONT reads, which are not yet deposited (gap type 1); the currently reachable entry point is the Zenodo Bambu quantification deposit.

capture_claim_note: env_lock_claimed: the paper's Rigor and Reproducibility statement claims a Singularity container encapsulating specific software versions, with access instructions in the repo, and the repo ships a .def build recipe plus a pull script. It is NOT container_digest_claimed because the analysis image is pulled by a mutable dated tag (:2025-03-04) rather than by digest, and it is not release_snapshot because no dated CRAN/Bioconductor snapshot is declared. At Stage 1 this is a claim only; version stays <= 1 on every step.
